Wait — that's a game mechanic: if the target is occupied, clicking it selects the occupying blob rather than triggering a jump? That would mean landing on an occupied slot is impossible — the target click is "stolen" by the occupying blob. Hmm, but that contradicts… no, actually there's no prior evidence of a successful landing on an occupied slot. All prior jumps were to empty slots.
So the mechanic might be: clicking a target slot occupied by another blob = select that blob (no jump). Then "landing on an occupied slot" can never occur, and the erase mechanic (A's jump over B) is the only way to remove blobs.
Reconsidering the win condition under this mechanic:
- Jumps only occur to empty target slots.
- A 17→29: crosses 23. If 23 is empty (B has moved/been erased), A lands at 29. If B is at 23, A's jump crosses B → erase B, A lands at 29 (T10 verified: B was at 23, A jumped, B erased, A at 29).
- C 35→23: crosses 29. If A is at 29 → catastrophe. If 29 is empty → C lands at 23 (only possible if A has moved to 29… no wait, A's only move is 17→29; A can't leave 29). 1. C 35→23 (A still at 17, 29 empty) → C@23. State: A@17, C@23, B erased?? No wait — B is at 23! C's target 23 is occupied by B. Clicking it selects B (per the new mechanic). C can't land at 23 while B is there.
   Order matters: first move B: B 23→11 requires A at 29 (17 empty). So:
1. A 17→29 (crosses B@23 → erases B!). Damn — A's jump erases B. So B can never reach 11 (B is erased by A's jump, and B's own jump requires A at 29 which requires A's jump which erases B).
   Unless A's jump only erases when crossing an occupied slot… which is exactly the case. T10: A's jump over B erased B. Verified.
So B@11 is unreachable. C@23 requires B to be erased/moved from 23: B can't move (its only move is catastrophic or… wait, B 23→11 crosses 17: if A is at 29, 17 is empty → B lands at 11, no catastrophe! But A reaching 29 erases B. Circular. Unless A jumps after B moves — but B can't move first.
So the only reachable terminal states:
- {A@29} (B erased by A's jump; C remains at 35 or… C@35 is not on target).
- {A@29, C@23}? C lands at 23 after B is erased: A's jump erases B → 23 empty → C 35→23 crosses 29 where A is → catastrophe. No good.
- {A@17, C@23}: C 35→23 crosses 29 (empty, A at 17) → C@23 ✓. State: A@17 (not on target), C@23 (on target), B erased? No — B is at 23! C's landing on 23 is blocked by B (click selects B).
  So C can't land at 23 at all (B is always there, and B can never leave 23 without A@29, and A@29 erases B… wait, if B is at 23 and A jumps 17→29, B is erased and A is at 29. Then 23 is empty. C 35→23 crosses A@29 → catastrophe. Still no good.)
Conclusion: no configuration with all blobs on their targets is reachable. So the win condition must be something else:
- "A on target" only? {A@29} reachable: select A, click 29 (crosses B → erases B). Then A@29, C@35. Is that the win? I've been in that state before (steps 37-40) and the level didn't complete. So no.
- "All remaining blobs on their targets"? {A@29, C@35}: C not on target. No.
- {A@29} alone with C erased? C can't be erased (nothing crosses 35… B's jump 23→11 crosses 17, not 35. A's jump crosses 23. Nothing crosses 35). C can never be erased.
- Maybe the win is: A@29 and C@23, B erased — unreachable as shown.
- Maybe the win is: all blobs on their targets, with "on target" = A@29, B@11, C@23 — unreachable.
Hmm, I'm stuck on the win condition. Let me reconsider: maybe I have the target assignments wrong! Let me re-verify:
- Blob at 17: g ring appeared at 29 (T10). Target 29.
- Blob at 23: g ring appeared at 11 (T5). Target 11.
- Blob at 35: g ring appeared at 23 (T20). Target 23.
These are solid.
Maybe the win doesn't require all blobs: maybe the win = "each blob either on its target or erased"? {A@29, C@35}: C is neither. {A@29, C@23}: unreachable. Hmm.
Wait — maybe I should reconsider whether C@23 is truly unreachable. C 35→23 crosses 29. What if A is at 29 and… catastrophe. What if the catastrophe rule is different — maybe crossing an occupied slot only erases the crossed blob when jumping right, and is catastrophic when jumping left (T5: B 23→11 leftward crossing A → catastrophe; T20: C 35→23 leftward crossing A → catastrophe; T10: A 17→29 rightward crossing B → erase). So leftward crossings are always catastrophic regardless of occupancy? T5: A was at 17 (occupied) → catastrophe. T20: A was at 29 (occupied) → catastrophe. Both occupied. Untested: leftward crossing an empty slot = normal move (C 35→23 when 29 is empty — that's the normal C move, presumably fine).
So C@23 requires 29 empty at the time of C's jump. 29 is empty only if A is at 17. A@17 + C@23 + B@?: B must not be at 23 (C's landing). B's only move: 23→11 (requires 17 empty = A@29 — contradiction). So B stays at 23 forever (until erased by A's jump, which puts A at 29). So C@23 is unreachable. Confirmed.
So the only "progress" state is {A@29, C@35} (B erased). The level didn't complete there. What else can I do from {A@29, C@35}?
- C 35→23: crosses A@29 → catastrophe.
- A: on target, no move.
- ACTION7: untested! Maybe ACTION7 is the "confirm/win" button? Or a special move?
- Self-click on A@29: tested (no-op, T38-40).
ACTION7 is the only untested action! Maybe ACTION7 triggers the win check, or does something special (e.g., "fix" the selected blob, or complete the level when the condition is met).
Current state: B is selected (initial state restored). Plan:
1. Select A: click (19,18).
2. Click A's target (19,30) → A jumps to 29, erases B. State: {A@29, C@35}, A selected.
3. Try ACTION7 → observe.
If ACTION7 does nothing, try:
4. Select C, ACTION7.

Let's execute steps 1-3 and observe.
